brief:
IHG Hotels & Resorts faces a core strategic tension between scale ambition and brand coherence in an industry growing faster than the company's own fee-based earnings would suggest. While IHG has surpassed one million rooms and 6,700 hotels across 20 brands, it remains structurally behind Marriott and Hilton in scale, and its addition of luxury and lifestyle brands (Six Senses, Regent, Vignette Collection, Kimpton) into a portfolio historically built on mainstream and midscale strength (Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Crowne Plaza) creates real risk of brand dilution. Positioning a company known for approachable, franchise-driven mass-market hospitality as a credible luxury and lifestyle player, without eroding the trust that anchors its largest revenue base, is IHG's central brand problem.

This is compounded by industry-wide pricing pressure from both full-service global chains and alternative accommodation platforms like Airbnb, as well as strong regional competitors such as Jin Jiang and BTG in Asia, a market IHG is actively expanding into. Because roughly 73% of IHG's system rooms are franchised and revenue depends heavily on owner signings and royalty fees rather than owned assets, the company's growth is only as strong as its ability to convince hotel owners that new and existing brands deliver differentiated demand, not just added complexity to the portfolio.

The business problem, then, is twofold: first, how does IHG scale its luxury and lifestyle tier fast enough (six brands into Saudi Arabia by 2028, new launches like Noted Collection and Ruby) to compete credibly with Marriott's and Hilton's luxury depth, without diverting investment or attention from the essentials brands that generate the bulk of system revenue; and second, how does it translate a fragmented 20-brand architecture into a single, legible value proposition for both loyalty members and potential franchise owners, at a moment when RevPAR growth (+1.5% in 2025) is modest and competitive differentiation increasingly depends on personalization, AI-enabled service, and authentic local experience rather than portfolio breadth alone.
